stories.title: United Ireland referendum 'off the table' - Burnham
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said a referendum on a united Ireland "is off the table". Mr Burnham made the comments during his first official visit to Northern Ireland, where he is meeting Stormont political leaders. "I'm here, as I said earlier, to listen, and I will take a collaborative approach but some issues will be off the table, and that is one issue that will be off the table," Mr Burnham told reporters in Belfast. He added: "I think we’ve got to focus on bringing people together as best we can, and I think we’ve lived through a decade where there’s been a referendum on Brexit, we had Scottish independence just before it.

stories.title: HSE-run nursing home inspection found infection outbreak
stories.summary: An inspection by the Health Information and Quality Authority (HIQA) of a HSE-run nursing home based in Munster discovered the early start of an outbreak of infection which resulted in transmission from two residents to 11 residents and five staff. Inspectors who visited the centre in March were informed that two residents had been unwell and had symptoms of an infection 24-48 hours previously, but they were better. Following a review of the nursing notes, an immediate action was given to the staff nurse to inform public health that a possible outbreak of infection was in progress. According to the report the HSE did not follow infection prevention contol guidance.

stories.title: Minister, RSA, gardaí to meet on motorway road safety
stories.summary: Senior officials from the Departments of Transport and Justice, as well as gardaí, the Road Safety Authority and Transport Infrastructure Ireland, are to meet on Friday to discuss motorway road safety. The meeting at Leinster House follows a number of recent incidents on the country's motorway network and will be hosted by the Minister of State with responsibility for Road Safety Seán Canney. In a statement, Mr Canney said he wanted to bring key road safety partners together to discuss what can be done to improve safety on motorways. Mr Canney said it is "a complex issue which has many causes" and that it will "not be easily solved".

stories.title: Nvidia forecasts quarterly revenue above estimates
stories.summary: Nvidia has forecast a 70% jump in revenue next fiscal year, underscoring unabated demand for AI computing, while warning that shortages of memory components would continue to curb how quickly it can expand. The chip company's shares rose nearly 5% in extended trading on Wall Street last night, after having dipped over 1% initially. "AI has reached its inflection point. It's doing useful work. Its tokens are productive and profitable. Now, compute is revenue," Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang said. The outlook is likely to reassure investors who have questioned how long the AI spending surge can last after years of explosive growth.

The Kildare man, who is based in Cork, was last involved with a hurling squad back in 2011 when he was strength and conditioning coach with Tipperary - winning a Liam MacCarthy cup a year previous, in 2010. O’Brien was signed for £17m (€19.9m) from Lyon in the summer of 2024 after an impressive season at centre-back, making 32 appearances and scoring five goals. stories.title: Leinster have point to prove after Munster mauling
stories.summary: Leinster have learned their lesson ahead of their rematch with Munster in the Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship final on Saturday, according to head coach Sana Govender. Munster thrashed Leinster 39-19 when the sides met in the opening round robin game in Cork three weeks ago, although Munster head coach Matt Brown believes his side caught Leinster "cold" in the seven-try hammering. The province rebounded with a 36-21 win against Connacht before a 75-5 stroll against Ulster to book their place in the decider, and get a shot at revenge against the defending champions, who also beat them in the final in 2025. And their head coach believes they have learned a lot since their defeat in Cork earlier this month.

stories.title: Dublin Fringe: How do you turn Kafka into a show for children?
stories.summary: Theatre Lovett take a joyful journey into the world of Franz Kafka for the Dublin Fringe Festival this September, with their latest family show, Kafka's Doll - Louis Lovett introduces a tale of love and loss, packed with songs, music, circus, juggling, puppetry, unicycling... and a pinch of magic. Franz Kafka is famous for dark, strange and sometimes bewildering stories. So how on earth does Theatre Lovett turn Kafka into a show for children and families? Kafka loved jokes, games and laughter. His fiancée Dora remembered that he "made everything into a game" and that they laughed together all the time. He was also a great storyteller and entertainer. When Kafka once read The Trial aloud to friends before it was published, they reportedly laughed so much that Kafka himself had to stop reading. It is this playful, mischievous side of Kafka that inspired our new work, Kafka’s Doll.

stories.summary: Nearly 1,400 people, including almost 800 foreigners, are missing across Nepal and Tibet, authorities said, after a wall of mud and rock collapsed into a Himalayan river, sending catastrophic flash floods ⁠through towns and valleys. The devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have killed at least 359 people, Nepali police said today. Chinese state media had earlier reported three dead in Chinese-controlled Tibet, taking the total killed to at least 362. Rescuers used helicopters to search for survivors and drop emergency supplies to thousands cut off after the floods swept a rugged mountainous region thronged by trekkers and pilgrims linking Lhasa in Tibet with Nepal's capital of Kathmandu. A lake has formed at the site where the flood in Nepal occurred is rising and is at risk of bursting, the country's disaster authority said, as it appealed to residents and rescuers to stay away from the river banks. The blockage of a river yesterday led to the lake's formation, the authority said.

stories.title: Qatar prime minister pursues mediation in Tehran
stories.summary: The prime minister of US ally Qatar has visited Tehran ⁠in a bid to revive diplomacy as the US and Iran traded recriminations over Washington's latest sanctions drive, described by one Iranian official as "all-out economic war". A Gulf neighbour of Iran, Qatar has served as a back-channel negotiator for the warring parties and played a direct role in securing a June ceasefire that briefly led to a cessation of hostilities. The visit comes as the war nears its sixth month with fighting largely paused but no diplomatic breakthrough in sight. Both sides are at odds over control of the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for global oil supplies that Tehran has used as leverage.

Sloyan will be the man in charge with Yeats County legend O'Hara becoming his assistant. The pair were joint-managers for just one season but the county have moved to make the adjustment ahead of the 2027 campaign. A statement from Sligo Co Board read: "At a meeting of its County Committee last evening (Monday, 24 August 2026) Sligo GAA endorsed the management teams for its senior football and hurling and U20 football teams for 2027.

stories.title: WXV selection fight adds extra intrigue to Interpro final
stories.summary: Munster head coach Matt Brown believes Ireland's upcoming WXV Global Series will add an extra pinch of spice to Saturday’s Vodafone Women’s Interprovincial Championship final against Leinster in Galway. The defending champions are looking to extend a seven-game winning run across the last two seasons when they face their rivals in the decider this weekend, having thrashed Leinster 50-15 in the final a year ago. The 2025 championship was played in the shadow of the Rugby World Cup last year, with the provinces deprived of their internationals who were in national camp. The internationals have been made available to the provinces this year, however, as they look to build gametime ahead of the WXV Global Series campaign next month, which Ireland begin against USA in Tallaght on 20 September.

stories.title: Slí na Samhlaíochta - celebrating the legacy of Manchán Magan
stories.summary: Musical Director Simon O'Reilly introduces Slí na Samhlaíochta/The Way of Imagination, a live performance coming to the National Concert Hall this October that brings together spoken word, music, and visual art in an exploration of the concept of Tír na nÓg through the work of the late author, traveller, broadcaster and documentary maker Manchán Magan. Slí na Samhlaíochta began at the Hedge School Festival in Doolin in 2023, an event I co-founded to bring musicians, writers and visual artists together to create new work. For the closing performance, Manchán Magan brought a spoken-word piece inspired by Tír na nÓg and An Saol Eile, the Otherworld of Irish tradition. Myles O'Reilly and I created a live score around his words, while Crosby Dunkley developed the visuals that accompanied the performance. None of us expected the response. From the opening moments there was a stillness in the room that is difficult to describe. The audience seemed completely immersed and, afterwards, many spoke about how deeply they had been affected. I came away feeling we had created something that deserved another life.

stories.title: Govt in 'doom spiral' over energy crisis, Soc Dems say
stories.summary: The Government is caught in a "doom spiral" where it is "lurching" from crisis to crisis in its attempt to drive down energy costs, the Social Democrats have said. The party's deputy leader Cian O’Callaghan accused the Government of failing to set out a plan to address the energy crisis, claiming it is instead reacting to the "whims" of US President Donald Trump. He was speaking as the Cabinet agreed that cuts to excise duty on petrol and diesel will be phased out over a period from November to the end of February. Last week, the Government announced that it was pausing the increases in excise planned for September and October amid rising fuel prices.

stories.title: New levy for sustainable flood insurance fund proposed
stories.summary: Insurance Ireland is proposing a new levy of €24 per insured household to be placed into a "sustainable flood insurance fund" to address what it calls "Ireland's flood insurance protection gap". The levy is among a number of measures put forward in a report by the group representing insurers, which it said would allow homeowners to continue to access sustainable flood cover amid increased flooding risk due to climate change. It said the fund should be designed to ensure households in higher-risk areas can access flood insurance, where cover would otherwise be unavailable. Insurance Ireland said the Government could consider rebalancing existing insurance levies alongside the proposed new one that could allow its proposals to be introduced "with broadly no net additional cost to the average household".

Mr Harris said the excise cuts were costing roughly around €100 million per month, which would be funded by running a smaller budget surplus. He also indicated that there would be further measures in the budget to combat fuel poverty.

Having dropped from a career-high 10th place in the World Golf Rankings in June 2023, the Cavan golfer currently languishes in 82nd place, and so could do with a good showing on home soil. Maguire birdie the first, the 10th, before a run of pars until the 16th, where she dropped a shot. stories.title: Waterford to hold open trials as Molumphy promises change
stories.summary: Waterford will hold open trials in November for their senior inter-county hurling panel as new boss Stephen Molumphy vowed to "develop the next generation of hurlers" in the county. Last month, Molumphy was confirmed as Peter Queally's successor. The 42-year-old, who won two Munster titles as a player for the Déise as well as a league title to go along with All-Star recognition in 2007, was appointed on a three-year term. On Monday evening, Waterford posted a lengthy statement from Molumphy on their social media platforms.
